title: Taxation without Public Service: Tianjin Meat Safety Regulation in the Republican Era
core_idea: Investigate the operation and public reception of government-run slaughterhouses in early twentieth-century Tianjin, focusing on the adoption of biomedical definitions of safe food, municipal laws governing slaughterhouse construction and operations, and how taxation and administrative practices shaped meat-safety governance.
tldr: Analyzes how biomedical food-safety criteria, municipal regulations, and administrative practices—especially taxation—interacted in the governance and public perception of municipal slaughterhouses in Republican-era Tianjin.
